title: Español para lectura
subtitle: The 1000 most useful Spanish words · Latin American usage · for a Hebrew and English speaker
how: This book is for reading away from a screen. Frequency decided which words are in it; theme decides the page order, because a page about food is easier to absorb than a page of unrelated rank-neighbours.

Section G comes first and is not a word list. It covers the dozen function words that sit at the very top of every Spanish frequency list — que, se, por, para, lo. These cannot be learned from a gloss, so they get explained instead.
Nouns always appear with their article, because el/la is part of the word. Verbs appear as infinitives; the ones whose forms you cannot guess carry a present-tense strip.
Hebrew appears only where English is not enough — where one Spanish word needs two distinct English senses, or where English collapses a distinction that Hebrew keeps.
Appendix A lists words you already know. They are frequent enough to belong in a top-1000 list and transparent enough that spending a full entry on them would be a waste of your attention.
